payload.brief: Create a software to turn my Markdown notes into a searchable static site with tags and backlinks.
payload.problem_statement: User needs a way to convert personal Markdown notes into a browsable, searchable static website that supports organizational features like tags and backlinks between notes.
goals: G1: Generate a static site from Markdown files that can be hosted without a backend server
G2: Implement full-text search functionality across all notes
G3: Support tag-based organization and filtering of notes
G4: Automatically detect and render backlinks between notes
G5: Preserve Markdown formatting and structure in the generated site
non_goals: NG2: Dynamic server-side rendering or database integration
NG4: Version control or change tracking beyond what exists in source files
NG5: Authentication or access control features

constraints.text: Output must be static HTML/CSS/JS that can be hosted on any web server
Must process standard Markdown syntax as input

assumptions.text: User has Markdown notes stored as individual files in a file system
Backlinks follow a standard notation (e.g., [[note-name]] or similar wiki-style syntax)
Tags are embedded in notes using a consistent format (e.g., #tag or frontmatter)
User wants client-side search rather than requiring a search service
Site will be used by a single user or small group without access control needs

open_questions.text: What is the expected volume of notes (number of files, total size)?
What specific Markdown flavor or extensions should be supported (CommonMark, GFM, etc.)?
Should the tool run as a CLI, GUI application, or build script?
What is the preferred hosting environment (GitHub Pages, Netlify, local server, etc.)?
Are there specific design or theming requirements for the generated site?
Should the tool watch for changes and auto-rebuild, or is manual regeneration acceptable?

success_metrics: SM1: All Markdown files successfully converted to HTML pages (100% conversion rate)
SM2: Search returns relevant results within 500ms for typical note collections
SM3: All backlinks correctly identified and rendered as clickable links
SM4: Tags accurately extracted and filterable with zero false negatives
SM5: Generated site loads and functions in modern browsers without errors
stakeholders: User (note author and primary site user)
Potential readers of the published notes

glossary.definition: A website consisting of fixed HTML, CSS, and JavaScript files that do not require server-side processing
A reference from one note to another, typically shown bidirectionally so each note displays which other notes link to it
A lightweight markup language using plain text formatting syntax that converts to HTML
A keyword or label attached to a note for categorization and filtering purposes
